evidence.excerpt: Previously developed guidelines for these practices have been developed for Bernalillo County and the City of Albuquerque such as the Bernalillo County Water Conservation Guidelines and the Design Process Manual (DPM)

Bioswale, Infiltration Trench, Stormwater Curb Extension, Raised Median, Stormwater Tree Pit with Grate, Stormwater Planter Box, Pervious Pavement, Permeable Check Dam, Stacked Stone Erosion Control Basin "Zuni Bowl", Stone Channel Plating, Contour Swale, Media Luna Flow Spreader
Requires permeable soils for infiltration in under 96 hours.
Intended to release water into the soil within 96 hours.
Bottom of trench should be at least 3' above seasonal high water table
If native soils have a minimum infiltration rate of < 0.1 inches per hour, supplemental drainage systems may be required.
Bioswales are linear stormwater management features used to convey, slow, and treat runoff
Pervious pavement refers to a wide variety of surfaces... that effectively treat, detains, and infiltrates stormwater runoff
Bioretention See 'Bioinfiltration.' which is more accurate for a New Mexico context.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Abbreviated GSI/LID digest for arid-climate implementation; references Bernalillo County Ordinance 2107-8 and DPM for quantitative design but does not include peak-flow methods, hydrologic software, or detailed storm sizing equations. Edition inferred from source PDF URL (March 2025). Pipeline excerpt repair removed 1 unlocated citation(s).

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Bernalillo County GSI digest emphasizes desert bioinfiltration (bioswales/rain gardens) with supplemental irrigation; quantitative WQV sizing deferred to Ordinance 2107-8 and DPM. Infiltration practices reference 96-hour drawdown/infiltration timing and 3 ft SHWT clearance for trenches. Permeable pavement cites 0.1 in/hr native soil threshold for supplemental drainage; base/sub-base layer mins (4 in, 6 in) are separate components, not a single storage depth.
